speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with a chronic cough, weight loss, and generalized weakness; to begin my assessment, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 68-year-old male. The patient reports having a fever, cough, weakness, night sweats, and poor appetite persisting for 6 months. He has lost 7.5 kg (16.5 lb) over this period. No history of breathlessness, nasal discharge, nasal obstruction, palpitations, chest pain, or digestive symptoms. Released from prison 9 months ago after a 2-year sentence.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a significant weight loss accompanied by fever, night sweats, and a 6-month history of cough. Given your recent release from prison, have you had any close contact with individuals who have tuberculosis or similar respiratory illnesses?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Chronic cough and fever. I also have Weight loss, Night sweats, Generalized weakness, Poor appetite.

speaker: Doctor
text: The constellation of fever, night sweats, weight loss, and chronic cough over six months is highly concerning for tuberculosis. Given your recent prison sentence, you are at high risk. REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray. REQUEST TEST: Sputum_AFB_Stain. Do you have a history of HIV or any other chronic medical conditions?

text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pulmonary Tuberculosis.
